_readme: WHAT EACH PARTY PLAY ROUTE DOES WHILE THE SHARED PLAYER SCREEN HOLDS RENDERING (gh#272).
The screen holds rendering from its mount until its handover (player-screen.ts isRenderHeld,
and the data-render-hold attribute on <html>). A route either follows the hold -- 'adapter',
its code subscribes with onRenderHold -- or declares 'none' with the reason it does not.
ONE HOME, TWO READERS. scripts/render-suspension-check.mjs owns what syntax can prove: every
route has an entry, every 'none' has a reason, and every 'adapter' route's code subscribes.
scripts/webgl-pixels-probe.mjs owns what only a browser can prove: on EVERY party play route it
records each WebGL context the page creates, whatever expression asked for it, and counts every
WebGL draw call made while the page reads held. A route that creates a WebGL context while
declared 'none', or draws while held, FAILS there. Owner ruling 2026-10-17: the WebGL routes
suspend, every other route declares.
EXTENSIONS (gh#272 REFUTE round 2). Every entry lists the WebGL extension names its route may
request, lowercase. The probe books every getExtension request by name, whether it succeeded or
not, and FAILS a route that asked for one its list does not hold; a listed extension that draws
has its draw methods counted against the hold like the core ones. The lists were seeded by
MEASURING what each route requests on both legs of scripts/webgl-pixels-lane.sh (2026-10-17);
a library upgrade that asks for a new one reds there until this file admits it. The probe's own
WEBGL_debug_renderer_info request is booked apart and never charged to a route.
WEBGPU AND WORKERS. A WebGPU request on any route, or a Worker / SharedWorker on an adapter
route, FAILS unless its entry sets "webgpu": true / "workers": true. None does: the recorder
counts draws in this document only, so a render path outside it is refused, not trusted.
Adding or changing an entry is a reviewed decision about what that route does.
